# Stario

Stario is a Python framework for server-rendered hypermedia apps. Handlers are async functions that write HTML through a `Writer`. Routes are explicit `Route` values. Datastar morphs the page in the browser. A long-lived SSE stream keeps a screen live. State lives on the server. Stario is not ASGI; run it with `stario serve app.main:bootstrap` or `stario watch app.main:bootstrap`.

## Start here

- [AGENTS.md](https://stario.dev/AGENTS.md): the app guide. Copy it into every Stario repo. Layout, invariants, the CQRS default, render from state, signals, code shape, tests, common mistakes.
- [llms-full.txt](https://stario.dev/llms-full.txt): the guide and the three skills in one file, for tools that want more context.
- [The Stario way](https://stario.dev/docs/the-stario-way): the direction behind the rules.

## Skills (optional stacks)

- [stario-feature](https://stario.dev/skills/stario-feature/SKILL.md): add or remove one screen, step by step.
- [stario-litewriter](https://stario.dev/skills/stario-litewriter/SKILL.md): SQLite through `litewriter`; `watch` repaints the stream.
- [stario-tailwind-daisyui](https://stario.dev/skills/stario-tailwind-daisyui/SKILL.md): Tailwind v4 and DaisyUI with the standalone binary, no Node.

## Examples

- [chat-room](https://github.com/bobowski/stario/tree/main/examples/chat-room): the reference project tree.
- [tiles](https://github.com/bobowski/stario/tree/main/examples/tiles): single-file live board.

## Defaults in one paragraph

One folder per screen under `app/features/<screen>/` with `urls.py`, `views.py`, `handlers.py`, and `data.py` when the screen owns tables. A screen with no action is one `GET`. A screen with any action is `GET /page`, `GET /page/live`, and `POST` commands that reply 204 and publish. One `render(state)` returns the full document; the stream sends it again on each change. Signals hold form input only. Tests run through `TestClient(bootstrap)` and read the stream with `iter_events()`.
